fields.meta_title: Employee Benefits Survey Ranked by Value | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee benefits survey that shows which benefits your people value and what each one costs per user. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Benefits Survey That Shows What Staff Value
fields.hero_description: Name the benefits you pay for. Emergent writes an employee benefits survey that scores each one on awareness and value, with every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: Each piece below comes from one prompt that names your benefits and your renewal date.
fields.feature_1:
A 100-point question for trade-offs

Give each person 100 points to spread across your benefits. A total over 100 cannot be submitted. Nobody can mark every benefit essential, and the ranking shows real priorities.
fields.feature_2:
Awareness asked before value

Ask whether people know a benefit exists before asking how much they value it. A low score on a benefit nobody has heard of points to a communication gap, not a reason to cut it.
fields.feature_3:
Ratings for the plan each person holds

Upload enrollment from your benefits system or sync it by API. Each person then rates only the medical plan they hold, never a plan they have not been enrolled in this year.
fields.feature_4:
Cost per user beside every benefit

Enter each benefit's annual cost, and the dashboard divides it by the number of people who say they used it. Renewal talks with your broker start from a figure per person.
fields.feature_5:
Small groups stay out of the results

Set a minimum group size, such as five answers, and any team or location below it shows no results. People in a small office can answer about family leave without being singled out.
fields.feature_6:
The whole survey, exported to GitHub

Export the survey, its answer tables and its dashboards to your own repository. Next year, run the same items in the same order and compare each benefit's scores line by line.
fields.why_description: These platforms price per employee or per user and keep answers on their servers. Emergent builds your survey as an app you own.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Benefits Surveys HR Teams Run
fields.tab_content_1:
Staff spend their points on parental leave

Before next year's budget is set, 118 of the 140 people at a software company spread 100 points across eight benefits. Parental leave averages 22 points. The gym stipend the company already pays for averages 5, last of the eight, and the benefits lead takes both numbers into the budget meeting.
fields.tab_content_2:
Who has never heard of the EAP

Three weeks after enrollment closes, 312 employees answer five did-you-know questions about benefits they already have. The employee assistance program comes last: only 96 of the 312 knew it existed. The survey is confidential, and HR sends the EAP explainer to the 216 people who answered no.
fields.tab_content_3:
The commuter benefit at $4,000 per user

Finance uploads what each benefit cost last year, and 176 of 200 employees mark the ones they used. The commuter benefit cost $36,000 and nine people used it. It goes on the list of benefits to review with the broker.
fields.tab_content_4:
The HDHP rating your broker sees first

Every employee rates the medical plan they are enrolled in, matched from the enrollment file, on a 1-5 scale. The high-deductible plan averages 2.6 against 4.1 for the PPO, and 41 of its 63 comments mention the deductible. The broker gets both numbers before the renewal meeting.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Benefits Survey
fields.howto_description: Two of these steps happen before you write a single question, and the last two after the survey closes.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Work back from the renewal date
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List every benefit you pay for
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Say who can see each answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Find the date your broker needs decisions for next year's plans. Open the survey eight to ten weeks before it, while the results can still change what you buy, and keep it open for two weeks.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pull the list from your broker's summary and your payroll deductions, including the small ones: commuter, wellness app, pet insurance. A benefit left off the survey gets renewed by default, whether or not anyone uses it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: For each benefit, ask whether people know it exists, whether they used it this year and what it is worth to them. Then add one trade-off question to turn a list of nice-to-haves into a ranking.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A confidential survey keeps names so HR can follow up, as with an explainer sent to people who missed a benefit. An anonymous one keeps none. Pick one, and state it on the first screen in plain words.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write who gets the survey, which plans it covers and the smallest group that can see results. Emergent turns that description into the questions and dashboards. Change either later by prompting, without starting over.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sort benefits by average points, then add cost per user beside each one. A benefit with few points and a high cost per user is the first candidate to change. A low-awareness benefit needs a better explanation first.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish a short summary before open enrollment that leads with what changes next year. Tie each change to the survey result behind it. When next year's survey opens, people will remember that their answers moved something.

plan.angle: Seven of the top 10 are national benchmark reports (SHRM, BLS, EBRI, KFF, Mercer) that say what other employers offer; the three builder pages (SmartSurvey, Formbricks, Selerix) are question lists. Neither tells a company what its own people use, value and would trade. This page shows the survey a benefits team runs before renewal or after open enrollment: a points-allocation question for trade-offs, awareness items, plan-by-plan satisfaction and results split by shift and language, all owned as an app.
tab_stories: A 140-person software company asks staff to split 100 points across eight benefits before next year's budget, and paid parental leave outscores the gym stipend it currently pays for.
Three weeks after open enrollment, a short awareness check finds that the employee assistance program is the benefit fewest people know about, and HR sends an explainer to everyone who answered no.
Finance uploads what each benefit cost last year, staff mark the benefits they used, and the commuter benefit works out to $4,000 per user.
Employees rate the medical plan they are actually enrolled in, the high-deductible plan scores lowest, and the comments about the deductible go to the broker before the renewal meeting.
